image_description: A close-up, high-resolution photograph of a grey whale's head and upper body surfacing in green ocean water. The image prominently features the whale's small eye, mottled grey skin texture with white barnacle patches (callosities), and the arched rostrum. Water splashes around the lower edge, indicating movement.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a tight close-up of the side of the head/eye region. The top of the rostrum where blowholes are located is outside the frame or obscured by the angle. Cannot verify blowhole count or full rostrum shape.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The skin clearly exhibits the characteristic mottled grey pattern with distinct white/lighter patches consistent with barnacle encrustation and cyamids.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image only shows the anterior section of the whale. The dorsal area/posterior back is not visible in this crop.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Only a fragment of the body is visible. While the curvature suggests robustness, the full spindle shape cannot be verified from this close-up.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Consistent with the Head_and_Face checkpoint; the visible skin texture matches the description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and underwater/obscured. Baleen plates are internal structures not visible in this external shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are located ventrally and posterior to the head; they are not visible in this dorsal/lateral close-up of the head.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is completely out of frame.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The high-resolution detail allows verification of the rough skin texture and raised callosities (barnacle clusters).

selected_experts.reason: Primary verification that the subject is indeed a grey whale and not another cetacean species (e.g., humpback or right whale) based on skin texture and head shape.
To detect subtle AI artifacts such as unnatural blending between the whale's skin and the water, or inconsistent texture resolution in the barnacles.
To ensure the eye structure is anatomically coherent and the skin boundaries do not show 'melting' or topological errors common in AI generations of complex organic textures.

custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the eye structure; AI often generates distorted or non-concentric pupils in animals. Verify if the barnacle patterns look procedurally generated (repeating tiles) or naturally random. Check for any 'smearing' of the water foam into the skin texture.
